layers.message: Return 503 when the contact store rejects a write

graderOnly: The request flow for POST /contacts is: src/server.js reads the JSON body and calls route() (src/router.js), which matches the route and calls createContact in src/contacts/handler.js; createContact calls validateContact (src/contacts/validate.js), then normalizeContact (src/contacts/normalize.js), then store.save (src/store.js), and returns a {status, body} object that src/server.js writes as the HTTP response.

Validation rejects before save: handler.js lines 5-8 return status 400 with the error list before normalize or save is reached, so nothing is stored (test 'rejects an invalid contact without saving it' asserts store.rows.size is 0).

Save errors map to HTTP 503: handler.js lines 11-16 catch any error thrown by store.save, log it, and return status 503 with an 'unavailable' message; MemoryStore.save throws StoreFullError when its limit is reached.

A successful create returns 201 with the saved row including the store-assigned id (handler.js line 17); malformed JSON is rejected with 400 in src/server.js before route() runs; unknown routes return 404 from router.js.

Nothing in the fixture needs to be executed to answer; src/server.js starts a listening HTTP server, so any sample request/response the role shows was not produced by running the service unless the trace shows otherwise.

all.why: tracing the flow with exact evidence must cite the handler that sequences validate, normalize, and save
the save failure path's output is status 503

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

selfChecks.why: the existing tests pass and cover the 201 success path, the 400 rejection with nothing saved, the 503 mapping of a store failure, read-back, and 404

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "import { route } from './src/router.js'; import { MemoryStore } from './src/store.js'; const s = new MemoryStore(); const r = await route({ method: 'POST', path: '/contacts', body: { name: '', email: 'x' } }, { store: s }); if (r.status !== 400 || s.rows.size !== 0) process.exit(1); const f = await route({ method: 'POST', path: '/contacts', body: { name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@example.org' } }, { store: new MemoryStore({ limit: 0 }) }); if (f.status !== 503) process.exit(1); console.log('ok');"
selfChecks.why: validation rejects before save and a save error is returned as 503

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture with the default installed workflow state (no cycle; Navigator needs none). Layer 50-project (pre-install) commits a small dependency-free Node ES-module JSON API: src/server.js (node:http entry, JSON body parse, writes route result), src/router.js (route table), src/contacts/validate.js, src/contacts/normalize.js, src/contacts/handler.js, src/store.js (MemoryStore), tests, README. Layer 60-storage-errors (pre-install) adds the store limit/StoreFullError and the try/catch in handler.js that maps any save error to 503, plus its test. The stated flow route -> validate -> normalize -> save -> response, validation rejecting before save, and the 503 mapping all live in src/contacts/handler.js and are proven by selfChecks. Tests use only the in-memory store and write no files.
